## Confirming the drift

The scan fires two findings on the delete group — `crime_00009` (`action_label_drift`) and `crime_00010` (`copy_ia_drift`) — both anchored on `src/components/SeatList.tsx`, both reporting the same three aliases across the same three files. The source backs it up:

| File | Line | Label | href |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UserList.tsx` | 7 | "Delete user" | `/users/manage` |
| `UserList.tsx` | 8 | "Remove member" | `/users/manage` |
| `TeamList.tsx` | 6 | "Archive team" | `/teams/manage` |
| `TeamList.tsx` | 7 | "Delete the seat" | `/seats/manage` |
| `SeatList.tsx` | 6 | "Remove member" | `/seats/manage` |
| `SeatList.tsx` | 7 | "Archive member" | `/seats/manage` |

Two of the three files put **two different verbs on the same href** — `UserList` (both → `/users/manage`) and `SeatList` (both → `/seats/manage`). That's not a judgement call about product intent; it's the same destination labelled two ways in the same render, which is the strongest evidence in the fixture.

There's also a noun drift the scan *doesn't* report: user / member / seat. More on that below.

## Proposed canonical set

The decisive evidence for the verb choice is negative: there is no archive anywhere in this repo. `src/routes/` contains `admin.ts`, `billing-plans.ts`, `admin/billing-plans.ts`, `organisation.ts`, `teams.ts`, `workspace.ts` — no archive route, no restore flow, no soft-delete state. "Archive" is copy promising a reversible state that doesn't exist, so it's the alias to retire, not the one to standardise on.

| Intent | Canonical label | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Destroy the record | `Delete <noun>` | Default. Irreversible. |
| Detach from a collection, record survives elsewhere | `Remove <noun> from <collection>` | Only with the `from <collection>` clause — bare "Remove" is what caused this drift |
| Reversible soft-delete | `Archive <noun>` | **Banned until a restore path ships.** Nothing here implements one |

Nouns: `user` = the account, `member` = a user within a team, `seat` = a billing entitlement. Label the thing the button acts on.

Concrete rewrites:

- `UserList.tsx` — both rows target `/users/manage`, so they're one action. Collapse to a single `<NavItem label="Delete user" href="/users/manage" />`.
- `SeatList.tsx` — both rows target `/seats/manage`. Collapse to `<NavItem label="Delete seat" href="/seats/manage" />`.
- `TeamList.tsx` — genuinely two actions (two hrefs). `"Archive team"` → `"Delete team"`; `"Delete the seat"` → `"Delete seat"`. Note that second row duplicates `SeatList`'s destination and probably belongs there — a parallel-destination smell in miniature, adjacent to but not part of this finding.

## Which one first — and a caveat that changes the answer

**`UserList.tsx` first**, because it's the only file that already contains the canonical verb ("Delete") sitting next to a synonym for the *identical* href. Fixing it is a pure deletion of the contradictory row — no product decision, no route change — and it establishes the precedent the other two files are then mechanically rewritten against.

But sequencing here is a trap, and it's worth stating plainly: **the finding will disappear after step 1 while the drift is still there.** The detector requires ≥3 aliases each appearing in ≥2 files (`action-label-drift.ts:122-124`), and in this fixture every alias sits at *exactly* 2 files — the bare minimum. Drop "Remove" out of `UserList` and it falls to 1 file (SeatList only), leaving 2 qualifying aliases, and both findings clear — while `TeamList` still says "Archive team" and `SeatList` still says "Archive member". Any single-file fix produces that false all-clear, whichever file you pick.

So: treat this as one atomic three-file change. If you do sequence it, don't use a clean rescan as your done signal.

## How the two detectors differ on this fixture

**They don't.** `crime_00009` and `crime_00010` are identical in anchor file, group, alias list, per-alias file lists, and every score. The only differing field is `fix_shape` — "pick one verb per action; update labels uniformly" vs "pick the canonical label; redirect copies to it".

That's by construction. Both detectors call the same `analyse()` (`packages/core/src/detectors/action-label-drift.ts:71`); `copy_ia_drift` just passes `restrictToJsxLabel: true` (`copy-ia-drift.ts:36`), which does exactly two things:

1. drops labels whose `kind` isn't `jsx_*` — so `document_title`, `metadata_title`, `use_title` are excluded (`action-label-drift.ts:91`)
2. skips the `navEntries` loop entirely (`action-label-drift.ts:99`)

Neither restriction bites here. All six drifting labels are `label="…"` props on JSX `<NavItem>` elements, which the IA index classifies as `jsx_label` (`packages/core/src/ia/types.ts:56`) — they survive the filter. And `src/nav.ts:6-11`, the repo's only nav array, contains no delete-group token at all ("Teams", "Workspaces", "Organisations", "Admin Console"). Same inputs, same output.

The fixture exercises the shared path, not the divergence. To make them differ you'd need drift on a surface only the broader detector reads — e.g. add `{ href: "/seats", label: "Archive seat" }` to `src/nav.ts`, or a `useTitle("Remove member")` / Next `metadata.title`. Only `action_label_drift` would pick those up.

## Two things I'd change in the tool

Flagging these because they're about the detectors, not the fixture:

1. **Double-counting.** One problem is producing two low-severity findings with identical evidence, inflating `summary.total` from 11 to 12. Per the "signal over exhaustiveness" line in `CLAUDE.md`, `copy_ia_drift` should suppress when `action_label_drift` has already fired on the same `(group, anchor)` pair — or the fixture should gain a nav-only alias so the two findings genuinely diverge. The second option is better: it makes the fixture prove the detectors are distinct instead of assuming it.

2. **The noun drift is invisible.** The `user` group (`user` / `member` / `seat` / `account_user`, `action-label-drift.ts:54`) is drifting through these same three files and never fires. "member" appears in 2 files (UserList, SeatList) and qualifies; "user" appears only in UserList and "seat" only in TeamList, so each falls below the 2-file bar. One qualifying alias out of three needed. The ≥2-files-per-alias rule is doing sensible noise suppression on large repos, but on a three-component surface it hides drift that's plainly visible in the source.

No files changed — this was a proposal, as asked.
